configurePresets.description: Standard optimized release build for Linux/WSL with Highway SIMD and Ninja.

configurePresets.name: linux-debug

configurePresets.description: Debug build for Linux/WSL with debug symbols and Ninja.

configurePresets.name: linux-portable
configurePresets.description: Scalar reference build for Linux without SIMD.

configurePresets.name: wasm-release
configurePresets.description: WebAssembly release build for the Numkit IDE browser UI.

configurePresets.name: portable
configurePresets.description: Minimal build — all NUMKIT_WITH_* features OFF. Baseline reference that compiles anywhere; used for CI sanity and exotic platforms.

configurePresets.name: desktop-fast
configurePresets.description: Native desktop build for Windows/Linux x86_64. Enables Highway dynamic-dispatch SIMD — picks the best ISA (SSE4 / AVX2 / AVX-512 / …) at runtime on first call to any vectorised kernel.

configurePresets.name: apple-m
configurePresets.description: ARM64 macOS build. Targets Highway with NEON/SVE2 when the SIMD backends are implemented.

configurePresets.name: bench
configurePresets.description: Release build with NUMKIT_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=ON. Produces the numkit_bench executable for baseline performance numbers before any SIMD work.

configurePresets.name: bench-simd
configurePresets.description: desktop-fast preset plus NUMKIT_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=ON. Use this to compare against the plain 'bench' preset and measure SIMD speedups.

configurePresets.name: desktop-fast-threads
configurePresets.description: desktop-fast plus NUMKIT_WITH_THREADS=ON. Routes the elementwise SIMD kernels (+ - .* ./ abs sin cos exp log) through a persistent std::thread pool above per-kernel parallel thresholds; below the thresholds the kernels stay single-threaded. Bit-identical to desktop-fast for the supported ops.

configurePresets.name: bench-simd-threads
configurePresets.displayName: Bench with Highway SIMD + thread pool
configurePresets.description: bench-simd plus NUMKIT_WITH_THREADS=ON. Apples-to-apples comparison against bench-simd to see what multi-threading buys on the elementwise SIMD kernels.

configurePresets.name: browser
configurePresets.description: WebAssembly build for the Numkit IDE browser UI. Requires EMSDK env var pointing to an Emscripten SDK install. Uses the Emscripten toolchain file directly — no need to launch via emcmake if EMSDK is set. Highway is ON and targets WASM SIMD128 via -msimd128 -mrelaxed-simd; requires Chromium 91+ / Firefox 89+ / Safari 16.4+. Electron 33 (Chromium 130) supports this fully.

configurePresets.name: bench-clang
configurePresets.description: Drives the Visual Studio 17 2022 generator through the ClangCL toolset (clang-cl shipped with VS 2022 Professional). Highway is DISABLED — this preset exists to measure clang-cl's own autovectoriser and register allocator against MSVC's. On FFT in particular, clang-cl without Highway matches or beats MSVC *with* Highway, confirming the MSVC-codegen cliff documented in feedback_fft_msvc_limits.

configurePresets.name: bench-simd-clang
configurePresets.displayName: Bench with clang-cl toolset + Highway SIMD
configurePresets.description: Same matrix as bench-simd (NUMKIT_WITH_SIMD=ON) but compiled with clang-cl. Useful for measuring codegen + Highway integration differences against MSVC on the same machine. Requires VS 2022 Professional (ships clang-cl at VC/Tools/Llvm/x64/bin/clang-cl.exe).

configurePresets.name: bench-wasm
configurePresets.description: WebAssembly benchmark build. Enables Highway WASM-SIMD128 backend and compiles the numkit_bench Google-Benchmark driver for Node.js. Run after building with: node build-bench-wasm/benchmarks/numkit_bench.js

configurePresets.name: browser-threads
configurePresets.description: Same as 'browser' but adds Emscripten pthreads. Each pthread becomes a Web Worker; shared memory uses SharedArrayBuffer + Atomics. Requires the host page to be served with COOP=same-origin and COEP=require-corp (or to run in Electron with sharedArrayBufferAvailable). PTHREAD_POOL_SIZE pre-spawns workers at startup so the parallel SIMD kernels don't pay Worker spawn latency. Memory is fixed-size (no growth) — em++ warns that ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH + pthread runs non-wasm code slowly because every access checks shared state; we trade growth for the perf.

configurePresets.name: bench-wasm-threads
configurePresets.description: Same as bench-wasm but enables Emscripten pthreads to run the Highway parallel-SIMD kernels across Web Workers. Apples-to-apples vs bench-wasm to see what threading buys on WASM. Run with: node --experimental-wasm-threads build-bench-wasm-threads/benchmarks/numkit_bench.js (recent Node has it on by default).

configurePresets.name: coverage
configurePresets.description: Source-based coverage build: Ninja + clang-cl with NUMKIT_COVERAGE=ON (Highway SIMD off, for clean line attribution). clang-cl drives the link so clang_rt.profile auto-links from -fprofile-instr-generate. Ninja needs the MSVC dev environment, so build via scripts/coverage.ps1 (it enters a VS Dev Shell first), which then runs numkit_gtest under LLVM_PROFILE_FILE and emits an llvm-cov report filtered to src/. Architecture-review risk #6.
